result.scope_note: The Emancipation Proclamation, issued January 1, 1863, declared slaves free in Confederate states not under Union control, including designated areas such as New Orleans (then under Union occupation but included as a symbolically conquered city). It did not apply to border states or areas already under Union control.

explanation.text: The January 1, 1863 Emancipation Proclamation issued in Washington, D.C., applied only in the ten states still in rebellion and explicitly exempted New Orleans and surrounding parishes as Union-controlled.
The Final Emancipation Proclamation designated areas in rebellion and areas under Union control, explicitly exempting the city of New Orleans and parishes in Louisiana from coverage.

excerpts.text: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only in the ten states that were still in rebellion on January 1, 1863, namely South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina.

Specific exemptions were stated for other areas under Union control on January 1, 1863, namely 48 counties that would soon become [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), seven other named counties of [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") including Berkeley county, which was soon added to West Virginia, [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") and 13 named parishes nearby.[[27]](#cite_note-28)
